 Order

This appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 have been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 13.08.2024 passed in MACC No.161/2023 by the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Badnagar, District Ujjain whereby compensation in the sum of Rs.54,000/- has been awarded to him.

sentences.text: As per the appellant, on 10.07.2022, he was going on a motorcycle from Badnagar to Gram Samar.

When he reached Bangred Petrol Pump, respondent No.1 drove vehicle bearing registration No.MP-09-WD-2076 of which he was the owner and which was insured with respondent No.2 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against his motorcycle as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment where he remained under treatment for a considerable period of time.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6122 2 MA-8805-2024 03.
Thereafter, the appellant filed claim application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of compensation to him on account of the accident suffered by him.
The application was contested by the non-applicants by filing their written statements to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.

sentences.text: This appeal for enhancement of amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that in the accident he had suffered grievous injuries.
He had been taken to the hospital for treatment where he underwent treatment for a long period of time.
Due to the accident, he had suffered a considerable amount of pain and had to undergo extreme hardships.
His family members also had to be involved in his treatment at all time.
Due to the accident, the appellant was unable to perform any work.
The amount which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal under various heads is quite inadequate.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant by way of compensation be enhanced appropriately.

05. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2, Insurance Company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
06. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
07. The record indicates that in the accident the appellant had suffered grievous injuries on various parts of his body.
He had been taken to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6122 3 MA-8805-2024 hospital for treatment.
He underwent treatment at the hospital for a considerable period of time.
In the accident, he had suffered extreme pain and also fracture on his body.
He had to incur heavy expenditure on his treatment and had to keep attendant with him and to take special diet.
Due to the accident, he was unable to perform his regular work.

Considering the nature of the accident, the injuries suffered by the appellant and in the available facts and circumstances of the case, in my opinion, the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal to the appellant is inadequate.

08. It is consequently held that the appellant shall be entitled for enhanced lump-sum amount of compensation in the sum of Rs.54,140/- to him which shall be payable to him along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application by him till date of payment.
09. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE Shilpa Akram Khan vs Suryajeet on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56779061/
